_meta.purpose: Treatment plans for diseases of crops the CNN does not cover. Gemini may match a photo to one of these conditions; the grower must confirm the symptoms ('Does your plant look like this?') before any product is shown. Products and doses come only from the linked TNAU pages.

excluded_from_tnau.listed_for: Mango, papaya and chilli powdery mildew
Mango and papaya powdery mildew, groundnut rust, coconut leaf blight

excluded_from_tnau.reason: Extremely hazardous soil insecticide; not suggested by this app.
Current registration status not verified; other listed options are shown.
Antibiotics; draft ban on agricultural use (Dec 2021). Not suggested.
Herbicide injection; the plan says to uproot infected plants instead.

Papaya___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery growth on the upper side of leaves, flower stalks and fruit; severe attack makes leaves yellow and drop.
care: Remove badly affected leaves and destroy them.
Give plants enough spacing for air movement.

Papaya___Ring_spot_virus.symptoms: Vein clearing, puckering and mottled, distorted leaves; circular concentric rings on the fruit.
care: Uproot affected plants immediately - virus-infected plants do not recover.
Do not grow cucurbits (pumpkin, gourds, cucumber) around the field.
For new plantings: raise seedlings under insect-proof net and grow sorghum or maize as a barrier crop first.

Papaya___Leaf_curl_virus.symptoms: Leaves curl, crinkle and roll inward and downward, become small and brittle; plants are stunted with no flowers or fruit.
care: Uproot affected plants - infected plants do not recover.
Do not grow tomato or tobacco near papaya (they share the virus).
Ask a local expert which insecticide is approved to control the whiteflies that spread it.

Banana___Yellow_sigatoka.symptoms: Oval leaf spots with light grey centres and a yellow halo that merge into large dried patches; leaves dry quickly.
care: Remove and destroy affected leaves.
Keep the field weed-free and remove extra suckers on time.
Provide drainage - waterlogging favours the disease.
TNAU: spray 3 times at 10-15 day intervals from the first leaf specks, with a sticking agent (e.g. teepol).

Banana___Bunchy_top_virus.symptoms: Dark green streaks along the leaf veins and midrib; new leaves are short, narrow and bunched at the top of the plant.
care: Uproot and destroy infected plants (with their suckers) - they do not recover.
Keep the field clean and weed-free so new infections are seen early.
Use only virus-free planting material for new plants.

Mango___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery growth on flowers, young leaves and small fruit; infected leaves and pea-sized fruit drop.
care: Remove and destroy badly affected flower panicles and leaves.
TNAU: first spray soon after flowering and a second one 15 days later.

Mango___Red_rust.symptoms: Rusty red, slightly raised circular spots on leaves and young twigs that join into irregular patches.
care: Prune out badly affected twigs.
Prune to let light and air into the canopy.

Mango___Anthracnose.symptoms: Small blister-like dark spots on leaves and twigs; young leaves and tender twigs wither and die back; black spots on fruit.
care: Prune out dead twigs and remove fallen infected leaves.
For fruit: TNAU recommends a hot-water dip (50-55°C for 15 minutes) before storage.

products.name: Pseudomonas fluorescens (FP 7)
products.dose: 5 g per litre of water, every 3 weeks from October

Brinjal___Cercospora_leaf_spot.symptoms: Yellowish angular to irregular leaf spots that turn greyish-brown; badly affected leaves drop early.
care: Remove and destroy affected leaves.
TNAU: the variety Pant Samrat resists both brinjal leaf spots.

Brinjal___Alternaria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Irregular brown leaf spots 4-8 mm wide, often with rings, that join to cover large parts of the leaf.
care: Remove and destroy affected leaves.
Water at the base of the plant, not over the leaves.

Chilli___Fruit_rot_and_die_back.symptoms: Tender twigs dry from the tip backwards (die-back); sunken, dark spots and rot on the fruit.
care: Cut out dried twigs and remove rotting fruit.
Next crop: use disease-free seed (TNAU: seed treatment with captan 4 g per kg of seed).
TNAU timing: spray just before flowering, at fruit formation, and a fortnight later.

Chilli___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery growth on the underside of leaves; leaves drop.
care: Remove badly affected leaves.
TNAU: three sprays at 15-day intervals from the first symptoms.

Chilli___Cercospora_leaf_spot.symptoms: Brown circular leaf spots with light grey centres and dark brown margins; badly infected leaves fall early.
care: Remove and destroy affected leaves.
TNAU: spray twice at 10-15 day intervals.

Chilli___Leaf_curl_virus.symptoms: Leaves curl towards the midrib and become deformed; plants are stunted and flower buds drop.
care: Uproot and destroy infected plants - they do not recover.
Grow 2-3 rows of maize or sorghum around the field to limit insects that spread the virus.
Next crop: use healthy seed and cover nursery beds with nylon net.

Rice___Blast.symptoms: Spindle-shaped leaf spots with grey centres and dark brown edges (starting as small bluish-green flecks) that can merge and dry the leaf.
care: Remove weed hosts from bunds and channels.
Avoid excess nitrogen fertiliser.
Next crop: TNAU resistant varieties include CO 51, CO 52, CO 53, ASD 18 and IR 64.

Rice___Brown_spot.symptoms: Oval, dark brown spots with a yellow halo on the leaves (like sesame seeds); spots join and the leaf dries.
care: Remove infected debris and weed hosts from the field.
Use slow-release nitrogen fertiliser.
TNAU: spray when the disease reaches grade 3; repeat after 15 days if needed.

Rice___Sheath_rot.symptoms: Greyish-brown spots on the uppermost leaf sheath around the young panicle; the panicle rots or does not emerge fully.
care: TNAU: apply gypsum 200 kg per acre in two splits.
Botanical option: spray neem oil 3% at boot leaf stage and 15 days later.
Next crop: moderately resistant varieties CO 55 or ADT 59.

products.name: Hexaconazole 0.5% GR
products.dose: 4 kg per acre (soil application at tillering)

Coconut___Leaf_blight.symptoms: Leaflets dry from the tip downwards and look charred or burnt.
care: Remove and destroy severely affected leaves.
TNAU: apply 200 g Pseudomonas fluorescens with 50 kg farmyard manure and 5 kg neem cake per palm per year.
TNAU timing: 2 sprays at a 45-day interval during summer.

Coconut___Bud_rot.symptoms: The youngest one or two leaves turn yellow and droop; the crown rots into a foul-smelling mass, mostly in the monsoon.
care: Act quickly - bud rot kills the palm. TNAU: remove all affected tissue from the crown, then drench the crown and cover the cut area with Bordeaux paste, protected from rain.
Spray the crowns of neighbouring palms as a precaution.
Provide good drainage and avoid overcrowded planting.

products.name: Copper oxychloride
products.dose: 0.25% (2.5 g per litre of water), crown drench

Groundnut___Rust.symptoms: Orange-brown pustules, first on the underside of the leaves; badly infected leaves dry up but stay on the plant.
care: Remove volunteer groundnut plants and crop debris.
TNAU: repeat the spray 15 days later if needed.
